title: Annual Board Examination Section A Simulator 2 (FBISE Class 12 Chemistry)
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity on the Pauling scale?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element with a Pauling value of 4.0.

questions.question: Why is sodium stored under kerosene oil or liquid paraffin in the laboratory?

options.B: It reacts rapidly with atmospheric oxygen and moisture to form oxides and hydroxides

questions.explanation: Sodium is highly electropositive and reacts vigorously with moisture and oxygen; hydrocarbons do not react with sodium.

questions.question: Silicones are synthetic polymers characterized by which repeating backbone unit?
questions.explanation: Silicones (polyorganosiloxanes) consist of repeating -[R₂Si-O]- units with high thermal stability and water-repellent properties.

questions.question: Phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃) acts as a reducing agent and is dibasic because its structure contains:

options.B: Two P-OH bonds and one direct non-ionizable P-H bond
options.C: One P-OH bond and two P-H bonds

questions.explanation: In H₃PO₃, phosphorus is bonded to one =O, two -OH groups, and one direct -H. The P-H hydrogen does not ionize but confers reducing power.

questions.question: Which interhalogen compound has a pentagonal bipyramidal geometry with sp³d³ hybridization?
questions.explanation: Iodine heptafluoride (IF₇) has 7 single bonds and zero lone pairs, giving a regular pentagonal bipyramidal geometry.

questions.question: What is the equivalent weight of KMnO₄ in acidic medium (Molecular mass = M)?
questions.explanation: Equivalent weight = Molecular mass / change in oxidation number = M / 5 (since Mn changes from +7 to +2).

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for (CH₃)₂CH-CH₂-CH(CH₃)₂?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has 5 carbons (pentane) with methyl substituents at carbons 2 and 4.

questions.question: Catalytic hydrogenation of an alkyne using Lindlar's catalyst (Pd deposited on CaCO₃ poisoned with quinoline or lead acetate) produces:
questions.explanation: Poisoned Lindlar's catalyst delivers both hydrogen atoms from the same face of the catalyst surface (syn-addition), yielding cis-alkenes.

questions.question: Which of the following polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons consists of two fused benzene rings sharing a common C-C bond?
questions.explanation: Naphthalene consists of two fused benzene rings, formula C₁₀H₈, with a resonance energy of 255 kJ/mol.

questions.question: Which alkyl halide reacts with alcoholic potassium cyanide (KCN) to form an alkane nitrile (R-C≡N), but with silver cyanide (AgCN) to form an isonitrile (R-N≡C)?

options.A: KCN is ionic releasing ambidentate CN⁻ that attacks via carbon; AgCN is largely covalent where nitrogen donates its lone pair

questions.explanation: K⁺CN⁻ is ionic, carbon attack is preferred; covalent Ag-C≡N binds through the unshared lone pair on nitrogen to form alkyl isocyanides (isonitriles).

questions.question: Which reagent is used to detect dangerous peroxides in old samples of diethyl ether?

options.A: Aqueous KI and starch solution (yielding a blue color) or acidified FeSO₄ + KCNS (red color)

questions.explanation: Peroxides oxidize I⁻ to free I₂ (blue starch complex) and Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ (deep red thiocyanate complex).

questions.question: Which of the following reagents selectively reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols without reducing carbon-carbon double bonds, esters, or carboxylic acids?
questions.explanation: NaBH₄ is a mild, selective hydride reducing agent that reduces aldehydes to 1° alcohols and ketones to 2° alcohols, leaving esters/acids/alkenes untouched.

questions.question: Vinegar is an aqueous solution containing approximately what percentage of acetic acid?
questions.explanation: Household vinegar is 4-8% ethanoic (acetic) acid in water, typically manufactured by oxidative fermentation of ethanol by Acetobacter aceti.

questions.question: The non-protein, heat-stable organic component required by certain conjugated enzymes (holoenzymes) for catalytic activity is termed a:
questions.explanation: Apoenzyme (protein portion) + Coenzyme/Cofactor (non-protein portion) = Holoenzyme (active catalytic complex).

questions.question: In the Sulfite pulping process, wood chips are cooked under pressure with a liquor containing:

options.A: Calcium or magnesium bisulfite [Ca(HSO₃)₂] and excess sulfur dioxide (SO₂)

questions.explanation: Acid sulfite pulping uses Ca(HSO₃)₂/SO₂ cooking liquor to produce easily bleachable pulp used in fine writing paper.

questions.question: In Mass Spectrometry, the peak corresponding to the intact, unfragmented ionized molecule produced by loss of one electron (M•⁺) is called the:
questions.explanation: The molecular ion peak (M•⁺) gives the exact molecular mass (m/z value) of the compound.

questions.question: High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) is manufactured under mild conditions (few atmospheres) using which coordination catalyst?
questions.explanation: Ziegler-Natta catalyst polymerizes ethene stereoregularly into unbranched, tightly packed linear chains with high crystallinity and tensile strength.
